faq.answer: No. Scarcity, housing insecurity, disability access, caregiving, unsafe work, migration, and mutual-aid obligations can produce the same priorities. Compare matched periods of access and responsibility before retaining a self-preservation subtype hypothesis.
faq.question: Do practical safety, warm alliances, and resource continuity prove this subtype?

faq.answer: Use similar workloads across a resource-secure period and an access-constrained period, and record whether observable behavior changes when the matched condition changes.
faq.question: What makes the self-preservation Type Six comparison fair?

faq.answer: flexible sharing after replenishment, support from several people, and relaxed limits when scarcity ends are formal counterexamples that should reduce confidence rather than be dismissed as exceptions.
faq.question: Which changed-resource counterexample weakens the safety-continuity hypothesis?

sections.body_md: Within a Type Six core hypothesis, the self-preservation subtype may emphasize practical safety, dependable resources, and warm alliances. Check material access and relationship conditions first, then keep the subtype idea secondary and revisable.
sections.title: State the tradition as a secondary testable idea

sections.body_md: Compare similar workloads during one resource-secure period and one period of constrained access. Record whether alliance seeking or contingency planning changes when supplies, housing, or reliable help are restored.
sections.title: Use matched situations before interpreting the pattern

sections.body_md: The self-preservation label organizes resource-continuity observations; it is not evidence about bodily mechanisms, neural systems, fixed functions, or a universal biological category.
sections.title: Reject bodily and neurological mechanism claims

sections.body_md: A person may host, share, or appear calm while managing real scarcity or caregiving duties. That visible style alone cannot prove or disprove a self-preservation subtype hypothesis.
sections.title: Allow behavior that looks unlike the stereotype

sections.body_md: Scarcity, housing insecurity, disability access, caregiving, unsafe work, migration, and mutual-aid obligations can shape the same response. Address those material realities directly rather than translating them into personality essence.
sections.title: Audit material, institutional, and relational conditions

sections.body_md: Lower confidence when the record shows flexible sharing after replenishment, support from several people, and relaxed limits when scarcity ends, and preserve the environmental account as a live alternative.
sections.title: Use changed conditions as a disconfirmation test

sections.body_md: Instrument-specific evidence cannot establish universal subtype ontology or cross-cultural equivalence, and this page cannot forecast safety, resource sufficiency, or future conduct.
sections.title: Keep subtype inference local and non-predictive

sections.body_md:
Duration: 5

Context: Compare one resource-secure week with one access-constrained week, then include a shared-supply decision under similar workload.

Observable signal: Record housing and supply continuity, access needs, caregiving duty, who offers support, the boundary requested, and whether it changes after replenishment.

Page-specific signal: Observe whether alliance seeking and contingency planning decrease when replacement supplies and reliable access are restored.

Alternative explanation: Test scarcity, housing insecurity, disability access, unsafe work, caregiving, and mutual-aid obligations before retaining a subtype account.

Reflection prompt: Identify the resource change that most clearly altered the safety plan, and lower the hypothesis if material continuity explains the shift.

seo.description: Type Six self-preservation is a traditional subtype hypothesis about attention to practical safety, warm alliances, and resource continuity. This pattern does not establish subtype because scarcity, housing insecurity, disability access, caregiving, unsafe work, and mutual-aid needs may shape the same behavior. Matched resource access, practical stakes, consent, and household power guide this comparison.
seo.title: Type Six self-preservation: a practical safety, warm alliances, and resource continuity hypothesis
